notes: A destination in a list answer.

The discovery server lists `disabled IS false AND world IS false`, `like_score DESC NULLS LAST, deployed_at DESC`, 100 rows. dcl-one also serves `deployment_id` and `exclude_from_ranking` (fields of decentraland/places@e660fbc2); the discovery server has no such columns.
`Math.min(limit, 100)`.
`total` is the count; the page is empty.
`intParam`: `Number('abc')` is not an integer, so `limit` is the default 100.
`intParam`: a negative number is not kept, so `limit` is the default 100.
`intParam`: `Number('x')` is not an integer, so `offset` is 0.
A position has no pattern check; `10;10` is a parcel no place has.
An owner has no pattern check; `lower(p.owner) = '0x123'` matches no row.
A creator address has no pattern check; the lowercased value matches no row.
`only_favorites` is true only as `true`; `maybe` is false and the list is the default list.
`only_highlighted` is true only as `true`; `yes` is false and the list is the default list.
`with_realms_detail` is true only as `true`; `x` is false and no item carries `realms_detail`.
`user_visits` is outside `ORDER_BY_VALUES`, so the order is `like_score`.
An `order_by` outside `ORDER_BY_VALUES` is `like_score`; an `order` other than `asc` is `desc`.

A like by a wallet whose voting power reaches `MIN_USER_ACTIVITY` (100) rewrites the place row's `like_score` (`buildUpdateLikesQuery`, entityInteractions.ts:149-156, the Wilson bound of :97-105) and the lists order on that column (`p.like_score DESC NULLS LAST, p.deployed_at DESC`, Place/model.ts:602-611; the discovery server reads the same column, `places-repository/component.ts:174-203`), so the order and the served value agree. The three listed places mirror `like_score` 0.5 (4 likes, 1 dislike); the `user` wallet's qualified like on `excluded` makes it the bound of (5, 1), which lists first, then the two at 0.5 by `id`.
Unknown parameters are not read.
`p.positions && positions`: a parcel of the place, not only its base position.
`positionsParam` reads every `positions` value; `disabled IS false` drops the closed place.
`names` lifts `world IS false`; `p.world_id = ANY(lowercased names)`.
`names` are lowercased before the match.
`only_highlighted` also lifts `world IS false`, so highlighted world rows would appear too.
The discovery server has no `only_excluded_from_ranking` parameter; the list is the default list.
`lower(p.owner) = lower($owner)`; with operated parcels from the LAND index the row's positions match too.
`search.length < MIN_SEARCH_LENGTH` (3) answers an empty list and a zero count without a query.
With `search` the SELECT appends `rank` (`ts_rank_cd`) to every item and sorts by it first; only the seeded title containing "Plaza" matches.
`with_realms_detail=true` adds `realms_detail` to every item.

`most_active` is its own route: 100 rows cut by `is_most_active_place DESC, like_score <order> NULLS LAST, deployed_at DESC` (the places on a hot scene's parcels lead, the rest follow), each row's `user_count` from the hot scene at its base position, sorted by `user_count` in memory in the requested direction (stable, so the cut's order breaks ties) and paged; `total` is the size of that set, at most 100. The harness has no presence snapshot and every seeded `user_count` is 0, so the set is the default list.

An `offset` greater than the number of hot scenes (the places with players, at most 100) answers `[]` with `total` 0 before the set is read. The harness has no presence snapshot and every seeded `user_count` is 0, so any positive offset is past the players; 100 is past the seeded set as well.
`only_favorites` without a user answers `{ data: [], total: 0 }`.
`search: params.get('search') ?? undefined` keeps the empty string, which is falsy: no length gate and no text query.
`multiParam` splits each value on commas and trims; `p.categories && {poi,game}` matches the plaza (poi) and the featured place (game).
`only_highlighted` is true only as `true`; `1` is false and the list is the default list.
`positions` applies only without `names` (`filters.positions?.length && !filters.names?.length`).

notes: getWorld passes the param verbatim to `WHERE w.id = $1`; the id is the lowercased name, so an upper-case name is a 404 (the social card route lowercases, this one does not).
`data` is an array of world_name strings ordered by world_name ASC, `total` their count; same show_in_places + enabled-place condition as /api/worlds. No ajv schema and no parameters.

placeUrl() builds on the default PLACES_BASE_URL https://decentraland.org/places, sets pathname /places/place/ and `position` with toCanonicalPosition's default glue '.', so 10,10 becomes 10.10. The `link` header is `<url>; rel=canonical`. description/og:image depend on the seeded description/image and are not asserted.
A uuid `id` (validator isUUID) wins over `position` and is read with findByIdWithAggregates.
findByIdWithAggregates has no disabled filter, so a disabled place still gets a card and canonical link; its title is not seeded, so only the link is asserted.

A non-uuid id is ignored and with no position nothing matches: the copies.social.place defaults are injected verbatim; replaceHelmetMetadata turns the placeholder `image` into twitter:image/og:image metas (no bare `image` meta) and injects `site`, `card`, `creator` as named metas; no `link` header is set. Upstream computes og:url as siteUrl() + originalUrl.slice(1) = https://decentraland.org/places/places/place/?id=not-a-uuid (doubled /places/); that value is not asserted and should not be reproduced.
No `link` header on the fallback.
toCanonicalPosition returns null outside the world limits, so no lookup happens and the fallback card is served.
worldUrl() sets pathname /places/world/ and `name` = world_name on the default PLACES_BASE_URL.
injectWorldMetadata reads `id` or `name` and lowercases it before the lookup.
The world card falls back to the same copies.social.place defaults as the place card; no `link` header.
